title: What Happens When You Get a Fever?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Fever' ('Most providers say a fever is either 100.0 F (37.8 C) or 100.4 F (38 C)'; 'it can be a sign that your immune system has been activated, often to fight an infection'; 'Make sure you drink plenty of fluids and get plenty of rest'; call your healthcare provider if an adult's fever rises above 103 F (39.4 C), or if it lingers longer than about three to four days): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/10880-fever

Merck Manual Consumer Version, 'Fever in Adults' ('Fever is an elevated body temperature that occurs when the body's thermostat (located in the hypothalamus in the brain) resets at a higher temperature, primarily in response to an infection'): https://www.merckmanuals.com/home/infections/biology-of-infectious-disease/fever-in-adults

Cleveland Clinic, 'Chills' ('Many people feel chilled when they have a fever'; 'Chills and fever often go together'; 'Chills are a sign that your body is trying to regulate its core temperature'; 'When you shiver, your muscles relax and contract. This involuntary movement warms your body'): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/21476-chills

NHS, 'High temperature (fever) in adults' (a high temperature is usually 38C or above; 'If you feel hot, cold or shivery, you may have a high temperature'; 'get lots of rest'; 'drink plenty of fluids (water is best) to avoid dehydration'; get an urgent GP appointment or contact NHS 111 if it's not getting better or is getting worse): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/fever-in-adults/
Tease (next video): NHS, 'Sunburn' (sunburnt skin may 'flake or peel – this usually happens a few days after you get sunburn'): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/sunburn/

lines.text: What happens when you get a fever?
Most doctors draw the line at one hundred point four degrees,
so why are you shivering like you're freezing?
When you're fighting off an infection,
your brain's thermostat resets to a higher temperature.
Your body has to catch up,
They tighten and relax, over and over,
and that movement is what warms you up.
lines.caps: AND THAT *MOVEMENT | IS WHAT *WARMS YOU UP

lines.text: Rest up and drink plenty of water,
and call a doctor if it tops one hundred and three
lines.caps: AND CALL A *DOCTOR | IF IT TOPS *103

lines.text: or drags on past three or four days.
Next Body File: what happens when you get a sunburn,
lines.caps: NEXT *BODY FILE | WHAT *HAPPENS WHEN | YOU GET A *SUNBURN

lines.text: and why your skin peels days later.
